- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day window, especially after a recent spike.
- Overestimates prices in the middle to late window, particularly when the true outcome shows a sharp upward trend.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after a significant price spike.
- Overshoots after a spike, then corrects with a downward bias in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model too quickly returns to prior levels after a spike, missing sustained momentum.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the first 5–7 days, then become more aggressive as the window progresses.
- When true price rises sharply, model fails to capture the full magnitude, especially in the first 10 days.
- Model exhibits a “late correction” bias — overestimates late in the window, then underestimates the final day.
